description: Jira CLI Foundation (Phases 0-2) — Go CLI wrapping Jira Cloud REST API v3 with auth, config, issue CRUD, and search

swaggerNotes: IssueBean.fields is additionalProperties (dynamic) in Swagger — field name for subtasks is NOT defined in the OpenAPI spec. Use json:"subtasks" tag (standard Jira convention); verify against live API response during integration testing
POST /search/jql returns only `id` by default — MUST send explicit `fields` param (e.g. ["*all"] or named list)
POST /issue returns {id, key, self} only — `self` is API URL (/rest/api/3/issue/12345), browse URL must be constructed client-side: https://{instance}/browse/{key}
GET /user/search returns a plain array []User (not wrapped in an envelope)
DELETE /issue?deleteSubtasks is a string param ("true"/"false"), not boolean
PUT /issue returns 200 if returnIssue=true query param, else 204 (we use 204 default)
PUT /assignee: accountId=null unassigns, accountId="-1" assigns to project default (not used in MVP)
nonGoals: Interactive prompts — all input via flags
OAuth/SSO — API tokens only
Issue comments as standalone commands — only via --comment on move
Boards, sprints, dashboards — future phases
Custom field type coercion — values sent as JSON strings
Attachments — future phases
Webhooks or event subscriptions
Server/Data Center API support — Cloud only
Bulk operations — single issue per command
Rich terminal UI (TUI) — tables and text only
Plugin/extension system — future
Import/export
Notifications
Time tracking
Worklog management
Project/board administration
Issue link creation/deletion — read-only display of existing links IS in scope (US-021b), but link mutation deferred to v2
Shell completions — Phase 5
goreleaser / CI/CD pipeline — Phase 6
jira schema, jira meta, jira project, jira user commands — Phase 4
Alias expansion at runtime — Phase 5 (this phase only stores aliases)
--verbose HTTP debug logging — Phase 5 (flag registered as no-op)
--template flag for Go template output formatting — Phase 5 (use --jq for now)
--json <field-names> (gh-style field selection) — --json is boolean-only; use --fields for API-level field selection
Stdin pipe for positional args (e.g. echo PROJ-123 | jira issue view -) — use xargs instead
Batch/multi-key positional args (e.g. jira issue view PROJ-123 PROJ-124) — single-key-only for clear error attribution
--idempotency-key for create operations — deferred; idempotency notes per command instead
--dry-run on auth commands (login, logout, switch) — silently ignored if passed, not an error
Fuzzy/levenshtein matching for transition names — substring match is the maximum fuzziness
Watch/unwatch — deferred to v2
resolvedDecisions: Credential chain: flags > env > profile (matches gh CLI pattern)
Token-based pagination for search (not legacy offset-based) — Jira deprecated startAt for /search/jql
--yes not --confirm for destructive operations (clearer, matches common CLIs)
--jq uses itchyny/gojq (pure Go, no CGo dependency)
Markdown-to-ADF via goldmark AST walking (not regex)
Write-to-temp-then-rename for config atomicity (not advisory locks — more portable)
JIRA_PAGER > PAGER > system default for pager chain
SuggestionsMinimumDistance=2 for Cobra typo suggestions
Error exit codes: unique per category (0-8) for machine consumption
--field values always sent as JSON strings (no client-side type inference)

User account ID detection: ^[0-9a-f]{24}$ (empirical pattern from Jira examples, e.g. 5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5). NOTE: Swagger allows maxLength:128 with no pattern constraint — this regex works today but is not spec-guaranteed. If Atlassian changes the format, this heuristic will need updating
Browse URL constructed client-side (API returns only self/API URL)
--no-pager is per-command (not global) — only on commands producing long output
--text flag overrides output.format:json config back to text mode
Transition matching: first match when multiple transitions to same target (API order, documented limitation)
Comment pagination: show last 20 comments (MVP limit, no full pagination)
issue list with no flags defaults to assignee=currentUser() AND resolution=Unresolved (developer-friendly, matches gh issue list)
--body-file stdin safety: no timeout (breaks legitimate pipes); TTY rejection + 10MB cap as guards. Applies to every command accepting --body-file
Issue edit --dry-run: full before/after diff (fetches current issue via GET, computes diff per field, shows field: old → new). Extra API call worthwhile for actionable output
default.project from config: --project flag > default.project config > error. Applies to issue create, issue list, and any --project command
jira search vs jira issue list: both exist. search is raw JQL power tool (positional arg); issue list is flag-based ergonomic tool. Both share same search API method and output formatting
--sort/--order on issue list: appends ORDER BY to composed JQL. Avoids forcing users to drop to --jql just to sort
--quiet flag: global for mutating commands. Suppresses success output (exit 0 is sufficient). Incompatible with --json and --jq
HTTP status codes: POST /issue returns 201; PUT /issue and DELETE /issue return 204. API client accepts 200/201/204 as success; skips body decode on 204
Null email handling: User.EmailAddress is *string. Text output omits email; JSON outputs null
Issue key validation: client-side before API call. Lowercase auto-uppercased. Numeric IDs accepted. Invalid formats rejected with clear error
technicalConsiderations: Cobra command tree: each command follows NewCmdXxx(f *factory.Factory) *cobra.Command pattern with XxxOptions struct; no init(), no global state
Jira API v3: use new endpoints — POST /rest/api/3/search/jql (not GET /rest/api/3/search), GET /rest/api/3/issue/createmeta/{proj}/issuetypes (not old createmeta)
Basic Auth: Authorization header is Basic base64(email:apitoken) via custom RoundTripper
ADF is mandatory: Jira v3 requires Atlassian Document Format for description and comment body fields; plain strings are rejected
Search pagination is token-based: no total field in response; --offset requires consume-and-discard strategy
deleteSubtasks is a string enum ("true"/"false"), not a boolean — send as ?deleteSubtasks=true query param string
Assignee uses accountId only: name and key fields are deprecated on Jira Cloud
IssueFields is dynamic: use typed struct for known fields, json.RawMessage for custom fields
Shared --body-file utility: stdin safety (TTY rejection, 10MB cap) implemented once in internal/cmd/shared/bodyfile.go, reused by create/edit
Shared issue key validation: ValidateIssueKeyOrID called at top of every issue subcommand RunE, before any API call
User.EmailAddress is *string (nullable): Jira privacy settings can mask it. All display code must handle nil
Retry exclusions: never retry 401 (not transient) or request timeouts (already waited 30s). Only 429 and 5xx
Config file safety: write-to-temp-then-rename pattern prevents corruption from concurrent processes or crashes mid-write
Single static binary: go build ./cmd/jira produces one binary named jira with no external runtime dependencies
HTTP status codes: POST /issue returns 201 (not 200); PUT /issue and DELETE /issue return 204 (no body). Client.Do() must accept 200/201/204 as success and skip body decode on 204
successMetrics: go build ./... compiles cleanly with zero warnings from go vet
go test ./... passes with >80% line coverage on internal/ packages
Full auth lifecycle works: login → status (valid) → switch → status → logout
Issue lifecycle works: create → view → edit → move → assign → delete
Search returns results via both jira search (raw JQL) and jira issue list (flag-based)
--json output parseable by jq for every command — mutation commands include ok:true
--jq inline filtering works for all commands producing JSON output
Exit codes match spec for every error category (0-8)
No ANSI codes in piped output (jira issue view PROJ-123 | cat is clean)
Structured errors include correct context and suggestions for agent self-correction
jira issue move PROJ-123 progress works (substring match to In Progress)
jira issue move PROJ-123 Done --resolution Fixed sets resolution atomically with transition
Typo suggestions work: jira isue view → Did you mean issue?
All tests use mocks — no external Jira instance required
technicalContext.dependencyChain: errors → iostreams → config → auth → api → output → factory → commands
functionalRequirements: FR-1: All output to stdout (data) or stderr (errors/warnings); never mixed
FR-2: Exit codes 0-8 per error category; non-CLIError wraps as GENERAL_ERROR exit 1
FR-3: --json produces machine-parseable JSON; text is default
FR-4: --jq implies --json; filters applied before output
FR-5: --quiet suppresses stdout on mutation success; still exits with correct code
FR-6: --dry-run validates without mutating; outputs preview
FR-7: Errors include code, message, context map, and actionable suggestion
FR-8: No command writes errors directly — all return error to main.go
FR-9: Auth resolved lazily — auth-free commands never trigger auth
FR-10: Config reads never fail on missing file (defaults applied)
FR-11: All mutation JSON includes ok:true; all list JSON uses {data:[], pagination:{}} envelope. Exception: --web on read commands uses {ok:true, url} since it performs a browser-open action
FR-12: Color disabled when: not TTY, --no-color, NO_COLOR env
FR-13: Pager disabled when: not TTY, --json, --no-pager (per-command flag)
FR-14: Instance URL normalized on storage (strip protocol, trailing slash, /rest/... suffix)
FR-15: Markdown→ADF conversion for all description/comment inputs
FR-16: --field key=value: split on first = only; value sent as JSON string (no type coercion)

userStories.title: CLI error system with CLIError type and constructors
userStories.description: As a CLI consumer, I want all errors to include a machine-readable code, message, context, and suggestion so I can self-correct.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/errors/errors.go defines CLIError struct with Code (ErrorCode), Message, Context (map[string]interface{}), Suggestion, ExitCode, Err (wrapped error)
CLIError implements error interface and supports errors.Is/errors.As unwrapping

Error codes defined as constants: GENERAL_ERROR, AUTH_ERROR, VALIDATION_ERROR, NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, RATE_LIMITED, INVALID_TRANSITION, MISSING_FIELD, UNKNOWN_TYPE, AMBIGUOUS_USER, NETWORK_ERROR, CONFLICT_ERROR
Exit codes: 0=success, 1=general, 2=auth, 3=validation, 4=not-found, 5=permission, 6=rate-limited, 7=network-error, 8=conflict

Constructor functions: NewAuthError, NewValidationError, NewNotFoundError, NewPermissionError, NewRateLimitError, NewTransitionError, NewMissingFieldError, NewUnknownTypeError, NewAmbiguousUserError, NewNetworkError, NewConflictError

Error context shapes: AMBIGUOUS_USER includes {matches: [{accountId, displayName, email}, ...]}, INVALID_TRANSITION includes {available: [{id, name, toStatus}, ...]}, NOT_FOUND includes {key: "..."} or {resource: "..."}, NETWORK_ERROR includes {instance: "..."}, MISSING_FIELD includes {field: "...", type: "..."}
JSON marshaling produces: {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "context": {...}, "suggestion": "..."}}
Tests: each constructor produces correct code, exit code, context shape, and JSON shape (table-driven)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Context shapes are critical for agent self-correction — each error constructor must populate structured context data, not just a flat message

userStories.title: Pagination helpers for token-based and offset-based APIs
userStories.description: As a developer, I need pagination utilities for both Jira's token-based search and offset-based endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/api/pagination.go defines PaginationMeta: Offset, Limit, Total (*int), HasNextPage

Token-based paginator for POST /search/jql: uses nextPageToken, stops when isLast, offset implemented as skip-N-results (PERF NOTE: offset=N fetches N+limit results from API and discards first N — warn to stderr when offset > 1000)
Offset-based paginator: passes startAt and maxResults query params, reads total from response
Raw-array paginator: for endpoints returning plain []T — infer has_next_page from len(results)==maxResults, total is nil
All return ([]T, *PaginationMeta, error) pattern
JSON envelope: {data:[], pagination:{offset, limit, total, has_next_page}}

Semantic note for agents: pagination.offset reflects the REQUESTED --offset value (skip count), not a server cursor. For token-based search, total is null (API does not provide it). For offset-based endpoints, total is server-reported. Agents should use has_next_page to decide whether to paginate further, not total
Tests: token-based multi-page, offset-based, raw-array, offset skip, single page, empty results
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Performance: token-based offset is consume-and-discard — large offsets cause proportionally large API load. Consider warning when offset > 1000.
